name: ZDAnalytics Connector
author: ZDAPPS - Desarollo de Apps Moviles

sections.description:
ZDAnalytics Connector lets you add Google Analytics 4 (GA4) and/or Google Tag Manager (GTM) to your WordPress site without editing theme files.

Important: Tracking is disabled by default. Enable it only after you have obtained explicit consent from your visitors (for example via a cookie banner). If consent mode is set to “Require consent”, tracking runs only if:
– The configured consent cookie is present with an affirmative value, OR
– An integration returns true through the zdac_user_has_consent filter.

External Services

This plugin can load scripts from third-party services:

1) Google Analytics 4 (gtag.js)
– Used for: Website analytics (page views, events, etc.)
– Data sent: Collected by Google Analytics from the visitor’s browser (e.g., page views, events, device/browser details; IP is anonymized by configuration).
– When: On page load, only if tracking is enabled and consent conditions are met.
– Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
– Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

2) Google Tag Manager (gtm.js / ns.html)
– Used for: Loading tags configured in your GTM container.
– Data sent: Determined by your GTM configuration; loaded from the visitor’s browser.
– When: On page load, only if tracking is enabled and consent conditions are met.
– Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
– Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip file to your WordPress site.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings → ZDAnalytics Connector and configure your IDs.
  4. Enable tracking only after you have set up consent.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin track users by default?

No. Tracking output is disabled by default. You must explicitly enable it in Settings.

How do I integrate with my cookie banner / consent plugin?

Option A: Set a consent cookie name in Settings and ensure your consent plugin sets that cookie when the user accepts.
Option B: Use the filter zdac_user_has_consent to return true when consent is granted.
